title: Smartphone-over-Microscope Diagnosis: Empowering Community Health Workers with TinyML for Malaria Parasite Detection in Rural Areas
summary: A Ghanaian research project proposes smartphone and TinyML support for malaria microscopy, with rural diagnostic access as its intended benefit.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The project combines microscope imagery, a smartphone, and a compact malaria-detection model. Its cited testbed is the Lacuna Malaria Detection Challenge, and further data collection with local clinics is planned. The proposed benefit is diagnostic support for community health workers. No field diagnosis or treatment outcome is reported.
purpose: Help community health workers identify malaria parasites with low-cost devices.

ratings.reason: The TinyML malaria workflow proposes diagnostic support for community health workers; no field performance or operational saving is reported.
No patient diagnosis, treatment change, or recovery is documented.
Expanded rural malaria care is a proposed public-health benefit.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 4: Smartphone-over-Microscope Diagnosis: Empowering Community Health Workers with TinyML for Malaria Parasite Detection in Rural Areas

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.
